source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 54
35 SILENT FORMATIONS | RANDOM VERIFICATION
Module A extension - transpose the five-form map to natural roots
ROOT NOTE -> ROOT STRING -> FORM FORMULA -> PRACTICAL FRAGMENT -> TRIAD
Draw one root and one form. Choose an octave where the formula remains on the neck. Form silently, name every root inside the voicing, sound one practical partial, and arpeggiate one embedded triad.
Root-fret command table Random formation sequence
Root C/A-form A root G/E-form low-E root D-form D root 1. Draw root and form.
C 3 / 15 8 10
2. State the root string and fret.
D 5 10 0 / 12
3. Calculate the form formula.
E 7 0 / 12 2 / 14
4. Name every root in the voicing.
F 8 1 / 13 3 / 15
G 10 3 / 15 5 / 17 5. Form silently and release.
A 0 / 12 5 / 17 7 6. Sound the practical partial.
B 2 / 14 7 9
7. Name and arpeggiate one triad inversion.
Natural-root prompt matrix
C C form A form G form E form D form
D C form A form G form E form D form
E C form A form G form E form D form
F C form A form G form E form D form
G C form A form G form E form D form
A C form A form G form E form D form
B C form A form G form E form D form
Do not judge success by whether the largest full grip can be held. Success means the root region, practical fragment, triad inversion, and local scale tones can be identified and used.
Standard tuning. CAGED is used as a practical root, chord, triad, arpeggio, and nearby-scale index. Page 18 of 20

steps.name: calculate_formula
steps.instruction: Calculate the printed form formula, including muted strings; name every root inside it.

steps.name: silent_formation
steps.instruction: Form silently and release before sounding the practical partial. Do not force the largest grip.

steps.name: manual_release
steps.instruction: Manually release fretting pressure and stop/mute the external source before continuing.

steps.name: choose_practical_partial
steps.instruction: Explicitly choose a practical partial from the calculated form.

steps.name: sound_practical_partial
steps.instruction: Sound the chosen practical partial; report this as your manual declaration.

steps.name: manual_release
steps.instruction: Manually release fretting pressure and stop/mute the external source before continuing.

steps.name: choose_embedded_triad
steps.instruction: Name a triad inversion and explicitly choose three contacts inside the calculated form.

steps.name: arpeggiate_embedded_triad
steps.instruction: Name and arpeggiate the chosen embedded triad inversion.

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 54
35 SILENT FORMATIONS | RANDOM VERIFICATION
Module A extension - transpose the five-form map to natural roots
ROOT NOTE -> ROOT STRING -> FORM FORMULA -> PRACTICAL FRAGMENT -> TRIAD
Draw one root and one form. Choose an octave where the formula remains on the neck. Form silently, name every root inside the voicing, sound one practical partial, and arpeggiate one embedded triad.
Root-fret command table Random formation sequence
Root C/A-form A root G/E-form low-E root D-form D root 1. Draw root and form.
C 3 / 15 8 10
2. State the root string and fret.
D 5 10 0 / 12
3. Calculate the form formula.
E 7 0 / 12 2 / 14
4. Name every root in the voicing.
F 8 1 / 13 3 / 15
G 10 3 / 15 5 / 17 5. Form silently and release.
A 0 / 12 5 / 17 7 6. Sound the practical partial.
B 2 / 14 7 9
7. Name and arpeggiate one triad inversion.
Natural-root prompt matrix
C C form A form G form E form D form
D C form A form G form E form D form
E C form A form G form E form D form
F C form A form G form E form D form
G C form A form G form E form D form
A C form A form G form E form D form
B C form A form G form E form D form
Do not judge success by whether the largest full grip can be held. Success means the root region, practical fragment, triad inversion, and local scale tones can be identified and used.
Standard tuning. CAGED is used as a practical root, chord, triad, arpeggio, and nearby-scale index. Page 18 of 20

Module A extension - transpose the five-form map to natural roots
ROOT NOTE -> ROOT STRING -> FORM FORMULA -> PRACTICAL FRAGMENT -> TRIAD
Draw one root and one form. Choose an octave where the formula remains on the neck. Form silently, name every root inside the voicing, sound one practical partial, and arpeggiate one embedded triad.
Root-fret command table Random formation sequence
Root C/A-form A root G/E-form low-E root D-form D root 1. Draw root and form.
C 3 / 15 8 10
2. State the root string and fret.
D 5 10 0 / 12
3. Calculate the form formula.
E 7 0 / 12 2 / 14
4. Name every root in the voicing.
F 8 1 / 13 3 / 15
G 10 3 / 15 5 / 17 5. Form silently and release.
A 0 / 12 5 / 17 7 6. Sound the practical partial.
B 2 / 14 7 9
7. Name and arpeggiate one triad inversion.

C C form A form G form E form D form
D C form A form G form E form D form
E C form A form G form E form D form
F C form A form G form E form D form
G C form A form G form E form D form
A C form A form G form E form D form
B C form A form G form E form D form

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 54
35 SILENT FORMATIONS | RANDOM VERIFICATION
Module A extension - transpose the five-form map to natural roots
ROOT NOTE -> ROOT STRING -> FORM FORMULA -> PRACTICAL FRAGMENT -> TRIAD
Draw one root and one form. Choose an octave where the formula remains on the neck. Form silently, name every root inside the voicing, sound one practical partial, and arpeggiate one embedded triad.
Root-fret command table Random formation sequence
Root C/A-form A root G/E-form low-E root D-form D root 1. Draw root and form.
C 3 / 15 8 10
2. State the root string and fret.
D 5 10 0 / 12
3. Calculate the form formula.
E 7 0 / 12 2 / 14
4. Name every root in the voicing.
F 8 1 / 13 3 / 15
G 10 3 / 15 5 / 17 5. Form silently and release.
A 0 / 12 5 / 17 7 6. Sound the practical partial.
B 2 / 14 7 9
7. Name and arpeggiate one triad inversion.
Natural-root prompt matrix
C C form A form G form E form D form
D C form A form G form E form D form
E C form A form G form E form D form
F C form A form G form E form D form
G C form A form G form E form D form
A C form A form G form E form D form
B C form A form G form E form D form
Do not judge success by whether the largest full grip can be held. Success means the root region, practical fragment, triad inversion, and local scale tones can be identified and used.
Standard tuning. CAGED is used as a practical root, chord, triad, arpeggio, and nearby-scale index. Page 18 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 54
NEXT: DIATONIC HARMONY AND ROMAN NUMERALS
Practice progression, CAGED boundaries, mastery gate, and log
CAGED IS MASTERED WHEN IT SHORTENS THE PATH TO MUSIC
Ten-phase progression Boundaries and repair
1. Memorize root-string formulas. 6. Extract all five chord arpeggios. SHAPE WITHOUT ROOT name every root before sounding the form
2. Build the five C-major forms. 7. Connect nearby scale tones. FORCED FULL GRIP reduce to the practical partial or triad
LOST INVERSION name the lowest degree of the triad
3. Reduce every form to its practical fragment. 8. Move C through the complete cycle.
SCALE DETACHED start and finish on a chord tone
4. Arpeggiate all fifteen triads. 9. Play five C-F-G-C cells.
CYCLE PAUSE practice only the failing adjacent forms
5. Convert each region to C minor. 10. Complete random roots and the capstone. FRET SEARCH calculate from the root-string formula
Mastery gate before Level 55
Find all five CAGED regions for any natural root and name the root strings. Play all chord arpeggios, scale routes, the CAGED cycle, and five C-F-G-C cells.
Form every C-major reference, practical partial, and embedded triad without leakage. Complete at least 30 of 35 random root/form prompts on the first attempt.
Convert the primary triad in every region from major to minor by moving one voice. Perform the twenty-bar register capstone on two separate days without a form-search pause.
Practice log
Date Root / form Full or partial Triad / inv. BPM Clean? Weak link Next target
NEXT Level 55 harmonizes the major scale, names chord qualities by Roman numeral, and transposes common progression families.
Standard tuning. CAGED is used as a practical root, chord, triad, arpeggio, and nearby-scale index. Page 20 of 20

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 55
THEORY -> FORMATION -> FUNCTION -> TRANSPOSITION
Practice progression, error diagnosis, and functional ear training
REPAIR THE FIRST LAYER THAT FAILS
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Say W-W-H-W-W-W-H. WRONG QUALITY recite the fixed M-m-m-M-M-m-dim sequence
2. Recite I-ii-iii-IV-V-vi-vii°.
WRONG KEY NOTE say the key signature before spelling the chord
3. Spell all seven triads in C and G.
4. Add D, A, E, and F key families. ROMAN CASE ERROR uppercase major; lowercase minor; ° diminished
5. Play every harmonized triad ladder.
FUNCTION BLUR reduce to T-P-D-T and sustain one chord per bar
6. Learn I-IV-V-I in all six keys.
7. Add the five remaining progression families. TRANSPOSE ERROR keep numerals fixed; rebuild chord names from degree 1
8. Play the nearest-inversion voice-leading cells.
TRIAD FRET SEARCH name string set and inversion before forming
9. Complete the analysis and transposition page.
10. Perform the 24-bar circle capstone. CAPSTONE STOP loop the final I bar plus the next key's I bar
Functional ear-training loop
Play I for four beats, ii or IV for four beats, V or vii° for four beats, then I. Sing each root. Repeat with eyes closed and identify only the function family: tonic, predominant, dominant, tonic.
Pass Material Task
1 I-IV-V-I sing roots and name T-P-D-T
2 I-vi-IV-V hear vi as tonic-family color
3 ii-V-I-I hear predominant-dominant-tonic

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 56
42 SILENT SPELLINGS | 6 PRACTICE KEYS
Module A - natural-minor spelling, function families, and the raised seventh
NATURAL MINOR HAS NO LEADING TONE; THE RAISED SEVENTH IS A CONTROLLED HARMONIC ALTERATION
Natural-minor function families Quality and alteration sequence
Natural: i--ii°--III--iv--v--VI--VII
Family Degrees Job
Quality: m---dim--M----m---m--M---M
Tonic i, III, VI minor home, relative-major color, stable expansion
Raise b7 to 7:
Predominant ii°, iv, VI moves away from tonic and prepares dominant
v minor -> V major or V7
Weak dominant v, VII modal pull without a leading tone VII major -> vii° leading-tone triad
The raised seventh is not part of the natural-minor scale. It is introduced because the dominant
function needs a leading tone.
Strong dominant V, V7, vii° raised 7 creates semitone pull into i
Six-key minor route used in this level: D -> A -> E -> B -> F# -> C#
Minor key Signature Natural scale Relative major Raised 7
D 1 flat: Bb D E F G A Bb C F major C#
A no sharps or flats A B C D E F G C major G#
E 1 sharp: F# E F# G A B C D G major D#
B 2 sharps: F#, C# B C# D E F# G A D major A#
F# 3 sharps: F#, C#, G# F# G# A B C# D E A major E#
C# 4 sharps: F#, C#, G#, D# C# D# E F# G# A B E major B#
Relative-major recall Silent spelling command
A minor <-> C major For every key: say seven natural-minor notes, seven natural triads, natural v, raised-seventh V or V7,
E minor <-> G major and leading-tone vii°. Six keys x seven natural degrees = 42 core prompts.
B minor <-> D major
F# minor <-> A major
C# minor <-> E major
D minor <-> F major
Standard tuning. Natural-minor harmony, minor-key progressions, and raised-seventh dominant preparation. Page 2 of 20

source_payload.txt_excerpt:
Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 56
THEORY -> NATURAL FAMILY -> DOMINANT ALTERATION -> TRANSPOSITION
Practice progression, error diagnosis, and natural-v versus strong-V ear training
REPAIR THE FIRST LAYER THAT FAILS
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Say W-H-W-W-H-W-W. WRONG QUALITY recite m-dim-M-m-m-M-M
2. Recite i-ii°-III-iv-v-VI-VII.
RELATIVE-MAJOR DRIFT return to i and sing the minor third
3. Spell A and E natural-minor families.
4. Add B, F#, C#, and D minor. v / V CONFUSION name b7 or raised 7 before forming the chord
5. Play every natural-minor triad ladder.
THEORETICAL SPELLING write E# or B# when the key requires it
6. Compare natural v with raised V in every key.
7. Learn all six progression families. FUNCTION BLUR compare i-iv-v-i with i-iv-V-i
8. Play the nearest-inversion i-iv-V-i cells.
TRANSPOSE ERROR keep numerals fixed and rebuild from the new tonic
9. Complete the analysis and transposition page.
10. Perform the 24-bar minor-key capstone. CAPSTONE STOP loop the old i bar and the next key's i bar
Natural-v versus strong-V ear loop
Play i for four beats, iv for four beats, natural v for four beats, and i. Repeat with major V, then V7. Sing the seventh degree before each dominant chord. The raised version should create a clearer half-step return into
the tonic.
Pass Progression Task
1 i-iv-v-i hear modal, softer dominant pull
2 i-iv-V-i hear raised 7 create stronger return
3 i-iv-V7-i hear V7 add another active tendency tone
4 random key identify natural v or strong V before chord name
Advancement rule
Add a key only after its natural triads, raised seventh, strong V, and leading-tone diminished chord can be spelled without reference. Raise tempo after three clean cells; reduce to blocked triads when function becomes unclear.
Standard tuning. Natural-minor harmony, minor-key progressions, and raised-seventh dominant preparation. Page 19 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VI, Level 56
THEORY -> NATURAL FAMILY -> DOMINANT ALTERATION -> TRANSPOSITION
Practice progression, error diagnosis, and natural-v versus strong-V ear training
REPAIR THE FIRST LAYER THAT FAILS
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Say W-H-W-W-H-W-W. WRONG QUALITY recite m-dim-M-m-m-M-M
2. Recite i-ii°-III-iv-v-VI-VII.
RELATIVE-MAJOR DRIFT return to i and sing the minor third
3. Spell A and E natural-minor families.
4. Add B, F#, C#, and D minor. v / V CONFUSION name b7 or raised 7 before forming the chord
5. Play every natural-minor triad ladder.
THEORETICAL SPELLING write E# or B# when the key requires it
6. Compare natural v with raised V in every key.
7. Learn all six progression families. FUNCTION BLUR compare i-iv-v-i with i-iv-V-i
8. Play the nearest-inversion i-iv-V-i cells.
TRANSPOSE ERROR keep numerals fixed and rebuild from the new tonic
9. Complete the analysis and transposition page.
10. Perform the 24-bar minor-key capstone. CAPSTONE STOP loop the old i bar and the next key's i bar
Natural-v versus strong-V ear loop
Play i for four beats, iv for four beats, natural v for four beats, and i. Repeat with major V, then V7. Sing the seventh degree before each dominant chord. The raised version should create a clearer half-step return into
the tonic.
Pass Progression Task
1 i-iv-v-i hear modal, softer dominant pull
2 i-iv-V-i hear raised 7 create stronger return
3 i-iv-V7-i hear V7 add another active tendency tone
4 random key identify natural v or strong V before chord name
Advancement rule
Add a key only after its natural triads, raised seventh, strong V, and leading-tone diminished chord can be spelled without reference. Raise tempo after three clean cells; reduce to blocked triads when function becomes unclear.
Standard tuning. Natural-minor harmony, minor-key progressions, and raised-seventh dominant preparation. Page 19 of 20

NEXT: SIXTEENTH-NOTE RHYTHM GUITAR
Practice progression, mastery gate, completion audit, and log
ADVANCE WHEN QUALITY, FUNCTION, AND VOICE LEADING REMAIN CLEAR UNDER REDUCED PRESSURE
Ten-phase progression Mastery gate before Level 58
1. Spell four seventh qualities 6. Major ii-V-I in six keys Name formulas and spellings m7 versus m7b5 distinction
2. Form E-root families silently 7. Minor iiø-V-i in six keys 56 silent movable forms A7-D7-E7 shell form
3. Form A-root families silently 8. A-blues shell comping four quality changes at one root eight arpeggio scans
4. Play both quality ladders 9. Eight arpeggio scans six major ii-V-I keys major and minor capstones
5. Reduce to shells 10. Two sixteen-bar capstones six minor iiø-V-i keys two clean days
Advancement standard
Form every quality at random natural roots; play the guide-tone shells without fret searching; keep the major and minor cadences audible without roots; distinguish m7 from m7b5 by restoring the flat fifth; and
complete both capstones with relaxed pressure and correct muting on two separate days.
Practice log
Date Family / key Quality / cadence D/U BPM Clean? Weak voice / shape Next target
NEXT Level 58: sixteenth-note rhythm guitar, syncopation, dead strokes, ties, releases, and full-song comping capstone.
Standard tuning. Seventh chords, shell voicings, ii-V-I movement, and functional voice leading. Page 20 of 20

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 59
NEXT: SEVENTH-CHORD ARPEGGIOS
Practice progression, mastery gate, completion audit, and log
THE LINE IS SUCCESSFUL ONLY WHEN THE LISTENER CAN HEAR THE CHORD QUALITY AND INVERSION
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Silent formation commands 6. Five-note pick-cycle loops NOTES RING TOGETHER release each string after its note
ARPEGGIO LOSES QUALITY say 1-3-5 or 1-b3-5
2. C root-position families 7. Major and minor inversion cycles
INVERSION UNKNOWN name the bass role before playing
ECONOMY BECOMES STRUM separate attacks and reduce pick depth
3. C first and second inversions 8. Quality switches and permutations

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 59
48 SILENT FORMATIONS
Triad formula atlas, silent formation, and transposition commands
THE LOWEST STRING OF THE SET DEFINES THE INVERSION START
Set Major root Major 1st Major 2nd Minor root Minor 1st Minor 2nd
G-B-e r,r,r-2 r,r-1,r-1 r,r+1,r r,r-1,r-2 r,r,r r,r+1,r-1
D-G-B r,r-1,r-2 r,r-2,r-1 r,r,r r,r-2,r-2 r,r-1,r r,r,r-1
A-D-G r,r-1,r-3 r,r-2,r-2 r,r,r-1 r,r-2,r-3 r,r-1,r-1 r,r,r-2
E-A-D r,r-1,r-3 r,r-2,r-2 r,r,r-1 r,r-2,r-3 r,r-1,r-1 r,r,r-2
Silent C-family commands Silent A-family commands
For each string set: form C major root, first, and second inversion; then C minor root, first, and Repeat the complete command cycle for A major and A minor. Keep fingers within one
second inversion. Name the three notes and bass role before releasing. centimeter of the strings and verify the quality-defining third before moving.
4 sets x 2 qualities x 3 inversions = 24 formations 4 sets x 2 qualities x 3 inversions = 24 formations
COMMAND: root -> quality -> inversion -> string set TOTAL SILENT FORMATIONS = 48
Root-finding and transposition rule
Root position begins with the chord root on the lowest string. First inversion begins with the chord third or minor third. Second inversion begins with the chord fifth. Find that bass note first, then apply the
relative-fret formula for the string set.
Set Lowest open string Root command example Inversion command example
G-B-e G C root begins G5 C first begins E on G9
D-G-B D A root begins D7 A second begins E on D14
A-D-G A C root begins A3 C first begins E on A7
E-A-D E A root begins E5 A second begins E on E12
Standard tuning. Major and minor triad arpeggios, inversion starts, picking systems, and chord-tone connections. Page 2 of 20

48 SILENT FORMATIONS
Triad formula atlas, silent formation, and transposition commands
THE LOWEST STRING OF THE SET DEFINES THE INVERSION START
Set Major root Major 1st Major 2nd Minor root Minor 1st Minor 2nd
G-B-e r,r,r-2 r,r-1,r-1 r,r+1,r r,r-1,r-2 r,r,r r,r+1,r-1
D-G-B r,r-1,r-2 r,r-2,r-1 r,r,r r,r-2,r-2 r,r-1,r r,r,r-1
A-D-G r,r-1,r-3 r,r-2,r-2 r,r,r-1 r,r-2,r-3 r,r-1,r-1 r,r,r-2
E-A-D r,r-1,r-3 r,r-2,r-2 r,r,r-1 r,r-2,r-3 r,r-1,r-1 r,r,r-2
Silent C-family commands Silent A-family commands
For each string set: form C major root, first, and second inversion; then C minor root, first, and Repeat the complete command cycle for A major and A minor. Keep fingers within one
second inversion. Name the three notes and bass role before releasing. centimeter of the strings and verify the quality-defining third before moving.
4 sets x 2 qualities x 3 inversions = 24 formations 4 sets x 2 qualities x 3 inversions = 24 formations
COMMAND: root -> quality -> inversion -> string set TOTAL SILENT FORMATIONS = 48
Root-finding and transposition rule
Root position begins with the chord root on the lowest string. First inversion begins with the chord third or minor third. Second inversion begins with the chord fifth. Find that bass note first, then apply the
relative-fret formula for the string set.
Set Lowest open string Root command example Inversion command example

D-G-B D A root begins D7 A second begins E on D14

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 63
NEXT: LONG-FORM ARPEGGIO SOLO CONSTRUCTION
Practice progression, mastery gate, completion audit, and log
ADVANCE WHEN THE SYSTEM CAN CHANGE WITHOUT THE HARMONY OR TIME CHANGING
Ten-phase practice progression Error diagnosis
1. Crosspicked triad rolls 6. Four-string sweep bursts CROSSPICK STALLS isolate one inside/outside change
HYBRID IMBALANCE reduce pick volume; shorten finger motion
2. Direction and skip rolls 7. Four-system comparisons
SWEEP SOUNDS CHORDAL release each fret before next string
3. Hybrid triad rolls 8. Major/minor cadence routes
SKIPPED STRING RINGS mute with both hands; reduce pick depth
4. Hybrid seventh patterns 9. Endurance circuits
ENDURANCE COLLAPSES shorten work interval; keep rest equal
5. Three-string sweep bursts 10. Capstones and recording SYSTEM SWITCH LATE decide system before phrase begins
Mastery gate before Level 64
Complete all crosspicking and hybrid cells with equal tone and both pick starts. Complete all four endurance circuits for 30 clean seconds with equal rest.
Execute all three- and four-string sweep bursts without note overlap. Perform both sixteen-bar capstones without losing the key sequence.
Perform every four-system comparison at one stable tempo. Record major and minor performances with intentional system choice and successful recovery.
Play all twelve major/minor progression routes with the assigned systems.
Completion audit and practice log
8 crosspick rolls 8 direction cells 8 hybrid triads 8 hybrid seventh cells
12 triad sweeps 8 seventh sweeps 8 system comparisons 12 cadence routes
Date Focus System BPM Work/rest Clean? Weak motion Next target
NEXT Level 64 develops long-form arpeggio solo construction, secondary dominants, key changes, and system-aware phrase orchestration.

Guitar Exercises - Section VII, Level 63
MECHANICS BEFORE SPEED
Technique atlas, pick symbols, muting roles, and release timing
THE RIGHT-HAND SYSTEM CHANGES; THE NOTE DURATION AND CHORD IDENTITY DO NOT
System Attack map Best use Primary failure
Crosspicking D-U-D-U repeating rolls and irregular string order flat pick path catches a string
Hybrid P + m + a bass-plus-upper voices and wide skips finger volume does not match pick
3-string sweep D-D-D / U-U-U short triad burst notes ring together as a chord
4-string sweep D-D-D-D / U-U-U-U seventh-chord burst pick outruns fret release
Muting responsibilities Volume responsibilities
Fretting hand releases the completed string. Picking-hand palm or spare fingers silence lower Reduce pick volume until m and a can match it comfortably. Do not solve a weak finger-plucked
strings. The active note should be the only sustained pitch unless a printed pedal tone is note by snapping the string or tensing the hand.
intentional.
Sweep-release sequence Endurance boundary
FRET -> ATTACK -> RELEASE -> NEXT STRING Work intervals begin at 15 seconds. Rest for the same duration. Increase time only after tone
and muting remain unchanged through the final repetition.
one pitch at a time
